2026-09-10T03:25:45.9076041Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9076792Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9077444Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9079261Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9080060Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9081040Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9084085Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9087517Z >
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9111411Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9118732Z >
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9120499Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9122126Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9122506Z ### How to Use
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9122970Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9124290Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9126600Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9127034Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9128361Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9138463Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9140431Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9141571Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9142183Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9143293Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9145022Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9148348Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9155296Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9156839Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9157263Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9160352Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9162174Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9163320Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9165108Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9165514Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9166164Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9167350Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9168622Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9171293Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9172709Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9173112Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9173654Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9174478Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9177513Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9181031Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9181413Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9183019Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9184701Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9186365Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9186979Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9187898Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9190206Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9191855Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9192799Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9193204Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9194675Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9196445Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9196801Z ```bash
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9198313Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9200128Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9201528Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9202383Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9203191Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9205972Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9208579Z ```
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9210090Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9210595Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9214554Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9216660Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9220170Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9222206Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9225517Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9226735Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9227123Z ### Notes
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9227564Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9229077Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9232055Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9234518Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9238486Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9241053Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9243228Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9245160Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9246518Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9247318Z <github-context>

2026-09-10T03:25:45.9280382Z 
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9281117Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9283673Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9286042Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9287841Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9291003Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9295593Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9297617Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9299679Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9301299Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9303034Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
2026-09-10T03:25:45.9304925Z table.
